message.content:
Based on the search results, here is an overview of BMI (Body Mass Index) standards:

## What is BMI?

BMI is a calculated measure of body weight relative to height, used to screen for potential health risks and categorize weight status. It is calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared (kg/m²).

---

## Standard BMI Classification (WHO/NIH/CDC - for general adult populations)

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal/Healthy Weight | 18.5 to 24.9 |
| Overweight | 25.0 to 29.9 |
| Obesity Class I | 30.0 to 34.9 |
| Obesity Class II | 35.0 to 39.9 |
| Obesity Class III (Severe Obesity) | 40.0 or greater |

This standard is used by the **WHO**, **NIH**, and **CDC** for White, Hispanic, and Black individuals.

---

## Asian-Specific BMI Standards

Due to higher metabolic risk at lower body weights, **WHO and NIH guidelines for Asian populations** use lower thresholds:

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Normal | 18.5 to 22.9 |
| Overweight | 23.0 to 24.9 |
| Obese | 25.0 or greater |

Some Asian guidelines (e.g., Singapore) define:
- **Obese**: BMI ≥ 27.5 (high risk)
- **Overweight**: BMI 23.0–27.4 (moderate risk)

---

## China's Adult BMI Standards

According to China's **WS/T428-2013** standard:

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight (体重过低) | < 18.5 |
| Normal (体重正常) | 18.5 to 23.9 |
| Overweight (超重) | 24.0 to 27.9 |
| Obese (肥胖) | ≥ 28.0 |

---

## Special Populations

### Elderly (80+ years)
- Recommended BMI range: **22.0 to 26.9 kg/m²**
- The standard healthy range is adjusted upward due to different health risk profiles in advanced age

### Children and Teens
- BMI is calculated the same way but interpreted using **age and sex-specific percentiles**, not adult categories
- Different calculators and growth charts are used

---

## Important Limitations

BMI is a **screening tool**, not a diagnostic measure of body fat or health. It does not:
- Distinguish between muscle and fat
- Account for body composition, bone density, or fat distribution
- Apply directly to pregnant women, highly muscular athletes, or certain ethnic groups without adjustment

Healthcare providers typically use BMI alongside other measurements like **waist circumference**, **body fat percentage**, and individual health assessments for a complete evaluation.

---

## Clinical and Surgical Thresholds

For certain medical interventions:
- **Bariatric surgery (general)**: BMI ≥ 40, or BMI 35–39.9 with comorbidities
- **Bariatric surgery with diabetes**: BMI 30–34.9 may be considered
- **Asian patients for surgery**: Thresholds reduced by 2.5 kg/m² (e.g., BMI ≥ 32.5 for expedited assessment with diabetes)

Sources:
1. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/9464-body-mass-index-bmi
2. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/losing-weight/bmi-in-adults
3. https://www.myheart.org.sg/tools-resources/bmi-calculator/
4. https://www.uptodate.com/contents/image?imageKey=OBGYN%2F97661
5. http://www.nhc.gov.cn/ylyjs/s3573d/202412/4cf1905d32304c15ac3bc4446ddb83f1/files/f932c5c0004f4959b92613dd1024483c.pdf
6. http://dayi.org.cn/qa/279026
7. https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/mxfcrb/lnjk/202408/t20240823_295135.html
8. https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html
9. https://apps.who.int/nutrition/landscape/help.aspx?menu=0&helpid=420
10. https://www.boltpharmacy.co.uk/guide/low-bmi-gastric-sleeve
11. https://www.trimbodymd.com/faqs/zepbound-bmi-requirements/
12. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/who-new-bmi-classification-obesity-diagnosis-criteria.html
